0.long_answer: Paralytic shellfish poisoning (PSP) is the syndrome caused by the accumulation of the neurotoxin saxitoxin, which is produced by dinoflagellates, in bivalve mollusks. Shellfish, acting as filter feeders, accumulate saxitoxin during harmful algal blooms. When humans ingest contaminated shellfish, they may experience nausea, vomiting, and potentially severe neuromuscular symptoms including paralysis. There are four recognized syndromes of shellfish poisoning, and PSP is specifically linked to the presence of saxitoxin.
